# Better Auth with organizations

Email and password sign-in with Better Auth, plus organizations: an org switcher, member management and invite links.

Id `auth/better-auth-orgs`. It fills the Auth slot: a project makes one Auth choice, or none. Template: [`templates/auth/better-auth-orgs/`](../../templates/auth/better-auth-orgs/).

## What it is for

Everything in Better Auth, plus organizations: each user belongs to one or more, with roles (`owner`, `admin`, `member`), an organization switcher, member management at `/app/settings/members` and invite links. The session carries the active organization, so scope your data by it. With the email add-on, invitations are also emailed.

## Add it

When you create the project:

```sh
npm create efforge my-app -- --auth=better-auth-orgs
```

Add it to an existing project whose `auth` is `none`:

```sh
npx create-efforge add auth/better-auth-orgs
```

Auth needs a database. On a project without one, add a database and an ORM in the same command (any of them works):

```sh
npx create-efforge add database/postgres orm/drizzle auth/better-auth-orgs
```

## Needs

- A database, and with it an ORM ([Add it](#add-it) has the command).

## Conflicts with

Nothing.

## Service and layer

Your code asks for `Auth`, declared in `packages/core/src/Auth.ts`. It has one member:

- `currentSession`. Fails with `Unauthorized`.

`AuthLive` implements it, and `efforge add` puts it in `AppLayer` in `apps/web/src/server/layers.ts`.

- To test code that uses `Auth`, give it a test layer: `Layer.succeed(Auth, Auth.of({ ... }))`. See [Swap a layer to test](../testing.md).
- To change the provider, write another layer for `Auth` and use it in `layers.ts` in place of `AuthLive`.

## Files it edits

`efforge add` makes these edits with AST transforms (changes to the parsed code, not to its text), so it changes only what is listed and leaves the rest of each file alone.

### `packages/core/src/index.ts`

- Re-exports everything from `./Auth`.

### `apps/web/src/server/layers.ts`

- Imports `AuthLive` from `./auth-live`.
- Adds `AuthLive` to `AppLayer`, imported from `./auth-live`.

### `apps/web/src/server/routes.ts`

- Adds `authRoute` to `workerRoutes`.

### `packages/db/src/index.ts`

- Re-exports everything from `./auth-schema.ts`. Only with `orm=drizzle`.

### `apps/web/src/server/auth.ts`

- Adds the `organization()` plugin to Better Auth.

### `infra/alchemy.run.ts`

- Imports `* as Config` from `effect/Config`. Only with `infra=alchemy`.
- Declares `betterAuthSecret` and binds it to the Worker as `BETTER_AUTH_SECRET`. Only with `infra=alchemy`.
- Declares `betterAuthUrl` and binds it to the Worker as `BETTER_AUTH_URL`. Only with `infra=alchemy`.

### `.github/workflows/deploy.yml`

- Passes the `BETTER_AUTH_SECRET` secret to the deploy job. Only with `infra=alchemy`.

### `AGENTS.md`

- Adds the rules under [Rules it adds to AGENTS.md](#rules-it-adds-to-agentsmd).

### `apps/web/src/server/account.ts`

- Runs `requireSession` before every server function in the file.

### `apps/web/src/capabilities/registry.ts`

- Adds `auth` to `capabilities`.

### `apps/web/package.json`

- Adds the dependencies listed below.

### `pnpm-workspace.yaml`

- Pins the new dependencies in the `catalog`.

### `.env.example`

- Adds the environment variables listed below, each with its local value, or empty where it needs a real secret.

### `.dev.vars`

## Environment variables

- `BETTER_AUTH_SECRET`, for example `change-me-to-a-long-random-string`: Signs sessions and cookies (production: a Worker secret, `wrangler secret put BETTER_AUTH_SECRET` or the deploy env with Alchemy). Locally `dev-only-secret-replace-me-with-openssl-rand-base64-32`.
- `BETTER_AUTH_URL`, for example `https://app.example.com`: Public origin of the deployed app, used for redirects and trusted origins (a Worker var). When unset, the origin comes from each request (under pnpm dev, localhost on any port). Empty locally.

## Package scripts

None.

## Rules it adds to AGENTS.md

### Auth (Better Auth)

- Server: `apps/web/src/server/auth.ts` builds the Better Auth instance (`makeAuth`); `auth-live.ts` provides it and the `Auth` service from `@repo/core`. Read the session in Effect code through `Auth.currentSession`, never from cookies directly.
- `/api/auth/*` is served by `auth-route.ts` (a `workerRoutes` entry). Client: `authClient` in `apps/web/src/lib/auth-client.ts`.
- Route guard: `routes/app.tsx` redirects signed-out visitors to `/sign-in?redirect=...`; build redirects with `safeRedirect`, never from raw input.
- Server functions: every one requires a session through `.middleware([requireSession])` (`require-session.ts`), except the few on the `public` list of `efforge/server-fn-session` in `vite.config.ts`. A Worker route (a WebSocket upgrade) checks with `requireSocketSession` from `socket-session.ts`, which closes a socket without a session with 4401 "Not signed in". Keep `socket-session.ts` out of anything the browser loads.
- Start-up on Workers: never await a promise that outlives the request that made it, and never await one across requests. Better Auth finishes starting in a promise (`auth.$context`) that, under `pnpm dev`, loads a module (I/O owned by the request that started it). `auth-live.ts` hands it to `waitUntil` instead of awaiting it while building the layer: the layer is built once per isolate, so an await there makes every request that arrives meanwhile wait on another request's work, which workerd fails with "the Worker's code had hung", and a request that ends first would leave the promise cancelled. Keep layer construction synchronous; pass slow start-up work to `waitUntil`.

Only with `orm=drizzle`:

- Auth tables are in `packages/db/src/auth-schema.ts` (Drizzle); after changing Better Auth plugins regenerate the schema and generate a new migration in `packages/db/drizzle/`, never edit applied ones.

Only with `orm=effect-sql`:

- Auth tables are plain SQL in `packages/db/migrations/0002_auth.sql`; after changing Better Auth plugins add a new migration file, never edit applied ones.

Only with `infra=none`:

- `BETTER_AUTH_SECRET` signs sessions: set it as a Worker secret (`.dev.vars` locally, `wrangler secret put BETTER_AUTH_SECRET` in production). Never log or return it. `BETTER_AUTH_URL` is the public origin and always wins when set. Unset, Better Auth takes it from the request (under `pnpm dev`, from localhost on any port); set it to sign in from another host in development, such as a phone on your network or a tunnel.

Only with `infra=alchemy`:

- `BETTER_AUTH_SECRET` signs sessions: Alchemy passes it to the Worker from `.env` locally and from the deploy workflow secret in CI. Never log or return it. `BETTER_AUTH_URL` is the public origin and always wins when set. Unset, Better Auth takes it from the request (under `pnpm dev`, from localhost on any port); set it to sign in from another host in development, such as a phone on your network or a tunnel.

### Organizations

- The `organization()` plugin is enabled: members, roles (`owner`, `admin`, `member`) and invitations live in the `organization`, `member` and `invitation` tables.
- The session carries `activeOrganizationId`; new users are sent to `/onboarding` to create their first organization. Scope data by it.
- Member management is at `/app/settings/members`; invitations are accepted at `/accept-invite/$id` (the invite link is shown to the inviter, and with the `email` extra it is also emailed).
- Check roles on the server before changing another member's data; the UI hides controls but does not enforce permissions.

## Limits

- Under `pnpm dev`, sign-in works from `localhost` and `127.0.0.1` on any port. From another host (a LAN address, a tunnel), set `BETTER_AUTH_URL` to that origin.
